page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor is equipped with a large 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

This instance includes 5669 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable. In benchmark evaluations, the D96ds_v7 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 106,546.32 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 596.61 GB/sec. Its memory subsystem delivers strong read-only large block bandwidth of 348.8 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth of 137.99 GB/sec. The local storage and high-throughput architecture support intensive database operations, as evidenced by a Redis SET performance of 156.15 million operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 151.5 GB/sec.

The hardware profile is optimized for workloads requiring high-density compute combined with substantial local storage, such as relational databases, large-scale web serving, and multi-threaded data processing. While single-core performance sits in the average tier, the massive parallel execution capacity and AMX-driven instruction sets make it highly efficient for CPU-based machine learning tasks, including prompt processing for medium and large language models. The lack of a dedicated GPU is a tradeoff for deep learning training, but the instance offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for general-purpose enterprise applications.
